blind.description: A traditional woven winnowing basket or grain scoop with a curved rear wall, low sides, an open front lip, and two small looped handles on the rim. The interior is filled with golden-yellow grain or kernels alongside a patch of lighter pale chaff or husks near the front edge. The wicker weave is stylized with tan slats and darker brown binding bands. The geometry is continuous and solid with no floating, broken, or melted parts.
blind.from_above: A D-shaped or shovel-shaped woven basket with two small loop handles on opposite sides, filled with textured golden-orange grain and a lighter cream-colored patch near the straight open edge.
blind.height_vs_figure: About 7 to 9 inches tall (roughly one-eighth the height of the figure) and approximately 1.5 to 2 feet wide.
